Oxidation is a chemical reaction where a substance combines with oxygen from the air around us!

Ang oxidation ay isang kemikal na reaksyon kung saan ang isang sangkap ay nakikipagsama sa oksiheno mula sa hangin!
copy.bis:
Unsay mahitabo sa oxidation?

Ang oxidation usa ka kemikal nga reaksyon diin ang usa ka butang makig-uban sa oksiheno gikan sa hangin!

copy.en:
Which makes more oxygen, a big tree or a small potted plant?

Plants with more leaves and bigger sizes make more oxygen! So, one large tree makes much more oxygen than a small potted plant.
copy.tl:
Alin ang gumagawa ng mas maraming oxygen, malaking puno o maliit na halaman sa paso?

Ang halamang may mas maraming dahon at mas malaki ay gumagawa ng mas maraming oxygen! Kaya mas maraming oxygen ang malaking puno kaysa sa maliit na halaman sa paso.
copy.bis:
Hain ang makahimo og mas daghang oxygen, dako nga kahoy o gamay nga tanom sa paso?

Ang tanom nga adunay mas daghang dahon ug mas dako makahimo og mas daghang oxygen! Mao nga ang dakong kahoy makahimo og mas daghang oxygen kaysa sa gamay nga tanom sa paso.

copy.en:
Who first isolated the gas oxygen in 1774?

Joseph Priestley was one of the very first to isolate the gas oxygen in 1774! That was a very long time ago.
copy.tl:
Sino ang isa sa unang nakahiwalay ng gas na oxygen noong 1774?

Si Joseph Priestley ang isa sa mga unang nakahiwalay ng gas na oxygen noong 1774! Iyon ay napakatagal nang panahon.
copy.bis:
Kinsa ang usa sa unang nakalain sa gas nga oxygen niadtong 1774?

Si Joseph Priestley usa sa mga unang nakalain sa gas nga oxygen niadtong 1774! Kana dugay kaayo na nga panahon.

copy.en:
Can you get sunburned on a cloudy, cool day?

Yes! Even though ozone blocks a big part of the UV, some still passes through clouds. You can still get burned if you stay outside for a long time.
copy.tl:
Pwede ba tay mapaso sa araw kahit maulap at malamig?

Oo, pwede! Kahit hinaharang ng ozone ang malaking bahagi ng UV, may nakakalusot pa rin sa ulap. Mapapaso ka pa rin kung matagal kang nasa labas.
copy.bis:
Mapaso ba ta sa adlaw bisan dag-om ug bugnaw?

Oo, mapaso! Bisan gibabagan sa ozone ang dakong bahin sa UV, adunay UV nga makalusot gihapon sa panganod. Mapaso ka gihapon kung dugay ka sa gawas.

What is the difference between ozone and ordinary oxygen gas?

Ozone (O3) has three (3) oxygen atoms, while ordinary oxygen gas (O2) has only two!
copy.tl:
Ano ang pagkakaiba ng ozone at karaniwang oxygen gas?

Ang ozone (O3) ay may tatlong (3) atomo ng oxygen, samantalang ang karaniwang oxygen (O2) ay dalawa lang!
copy.bis:
Unsay kalainan sa ozone ug ordinaryong oxygen gas?

Ang ozone (O3) adunay tulo (3) ka atomo sa oxygen, samtang ang ordinaryong oxygen (O2) duha ra!

How does PAGASA watch out for typhoons and dangerous weather?

They use a network of Doppler radars across the Philippines! These radars help monitor typhoons, rainfall, and dangerous weather conditions in real time.

Paano binabantayan ng PAGASA ang mga bagyo at mapanganib na panahon?

Gumagamit sila ng network ng mga Doppler radar sa buong Pilipinas! Tinutulungan ng mga radar na ito na subaybayan ang mga bagyo, ulan, at mapanganib na panahon sa real-time.

Unsaon pagmonitor sa PAGASA sa mga bagyo ug peligroso nga panahon?

Naggamit sila og network sa mga Doppler radar sa tibuok Pilipinas! Kini nga mga radar nagtabang sa pagmonitor sa mga bagyo, ulan, ug peligrosong panahon sa real time.

copy.en:
Want to know if the next months will be wetter or drier?

Every three months, PAGASA releases a seasonal climate outlook! It tells us the expected weather to help farmers and everyone plan ahead.
copy.tl:
Gusto mo bang malaman kung mas maulan o mas tuyot sa susunod na mga buwan?

Bawat tatlong buwan, naglalabas ang PAGASA ng seasonal climate outlook! Ibinibigay nito ang inaasahang panahon para makapagplano ang mga magsasaka at iba pa.
copy.bis:
Gusto ba nimo mahibal-an kung mas ulanon o mas tuyot sa mga sunod nga buwan?

Matag tulo ka buwan, nagpagawas ang PAGASA og seasonal climate outlook! Naghatag kini sa gilauman nga panahon aron makaplanear ang mga mag-uuma ug uban pa.

PAGASA issues thunderstorm advisories in the Philippines so people can prepare ahead of time!

Sino ang nagbibigay ng babala tungkol sa thunderstorm sa Pilipinas?

Ang PAGASA ang nagbibigay ng thunderstorm advisories sa Pilipinas para makapaghanda ang mga tao!
copy.bis:
Kinsa ang naghatag og pasidaan bahin sa unos sa Pilipinas?

Ang PAGASA ang naghatag og thunderstorm advisories sa Pilipinas aron makaandam ang mga tawo!

A stingray only stings when it's accidentally stepped on, so shuffling your feet along the sand as you wade warns it away before you step on it.

Bakit dapat ikiskis ang paa sa mababaw na tubig?

Natutusok lang ng pagi ang tao kapag naapakan ito nang di-sinasadya, kaya ang pagkiskis ng paa sa buhangin habang naglalakad ay nagpapalayo rito bago pa ito maapakan.
copy.bis:
Nganong kinahanglan ikiskis ang tiil sa mabaw nga tubig?

Motusok lang ang pagi sa tawo kon matumban kini nga dili tinuyo, mao nga ang pagkiskis sa tiil sa balas samtang naglakaw makapahilayo niini sa dili pa kini matumban.

How do you find the pot in blindfolded pukpok-palayok?

You rely on your hearing and touch instead of sight to find the hanging clay pot!
copy.tl:
Paano mo mahahanap ang palayok sa bulag na pukpok-palayok?

Umaasa ka sa iyong pandinig at pandama sa halip na paningin para mahanap ang nakabitin na palayok!
copy.bis:
Unsaon nimo pagpangita ang palayok sa blindfolded pukpok-palayok?

Nagsalig ka sa imong pandungog ug paghikap imbes panan-aw aron makit-an ang nagbitay nga palayok!

Do flowers only grow in Baguio?

Nope! Flowers grow even in hot lowland places, like gumamela and santan. Baguio is just famous for having so many beautiful ones, thanks to Panagbenga!
copy.tl:
Sa Baguio lang ba tumutubo ang bulaklak?

Hindi! Tumutubo ang bulaklak kahit sa mainit na kapatagan, tulad ng gumamela at santan. Sikat lang ang Baguio dahil sa dami at ganda ng bulaklak doon, kaya may Panagbenga!
copy.bis:
Sa Baguio ra ba motubo ang bulak?

Dili! Motubo ang bulak bisan sa init nga kapatagan, sama sa gumamela ug santan. Bantog ra ang Baguio tungod sa kadaghan ug katahom sa mga bulak didto, mao nga naay Panagbenga!

Where does extra energy come from when you run?

When you play or run, your muscles burn through sugar fast, so your body releases glucagon to release extra sugar as fuel.
copy.tl:
Saan nanggagaling ang dagdag na lakas kapag tumatakbo ka?

Kapag naglalaro o tumatakbo ka, mabilis na nauubos ang asukal sa kalamnan mo, kaya naglalabas ang katawan ng glucagon para magbigay ng dagdag na asukal na gagamitin bilang gatong.
copy.bis:
Asa gikan ang dugang kusog kon magdagan ka?

Kung magdula o magdagan ka, paspas nga mahurot ang asukal sa imong kaunoran, mao nga mogawas ang glucagon aron mohatag og dugang asukal isip sugnod.

copy.en:

No! Insulin is actually a protein made by the body. Its job is to manage sugar levels, not to be sugar itself.
copy.tl:
Asukal ba ang insulin?

Hindi! Ang insulin ay protina (protein) na ginagawa ng katawan. Ang trabaho nito ay pamahalaan ang asukal, hindi maging asukal mismo.
copy.bis:
Asukal ba ang insulin?

Dili! Ang insulin usa ka protina (protein) nga gihimo sa lawas. Ang trabaho niini mao ang pagdumala sa asukal, dili ang mahimong asukal mismo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: ground up, then kneaded and baked in an oven
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain why physical changes are reversible, and chemical changes are irreversible
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes processes (grinding, kneading, baking) but does not explain physical vs. chemical changes or reversibility/irreversibility. It only touches on material changes without addressing the competency's core concept.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: baked in an oven
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe changes in properties of materials when exposed to certain changes in temperature, such as changes when wood or coal are burned
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions baking (temperature exposure) but does not describe changes in properties of materials when exposed to temperature changes, nor does it give an example like burning wood or coal. The focus is on bread-making, not property changes due to heat.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: ground up, then kneaded and baked
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how changes in solid materials make them useful, such as when they are shaped, pressed, hammered, joined, or cut
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions shaping/processing of a solid (wheat flour) but does not describe how changes in solid materials make them useful in the sense of shaped, pressed, hammered, joined, or cut. It is about food preparation, not the utility of changed solid materials.

copy.en: That pandesal in the basket started as wheat flour — a plant grain ground up, then kneaded and baked in an oven!
copy.tl: Ang pandesal na nasa basket ay nagmula sa harina ng trigo — isang butil ng halaman na giniling, masahin, at niluto sa hurno!
copy.bis: Ang pandesal sa basket naggikan sa harina sa trigo — usa ka lugas sa tanom nga giniling, masahon, ug giluto sa hudno!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The papaya tree has big, hand-shaped leaves clustered at the top of its trunk, spreading out like an umbrella.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the appearance and arrangement of papaya leaves but does not identify their role in getting water and nutrients from the soil, which is the core action of the competency.

copy.en: The papaya tree has big, hand-shaped leaves clustered at the top of its trunk, spreading out like an umbrella.
copy.tl: Ang papaya ay may malalaki at hugis-kamay na dahon na nakapunta sa itaas ng puno, na parang payong.
copy.bis: Ang kapayas adunay dagko ug morag-kamot nga mga dahon nga nagpundok sa ibabaw sa punoan, nga morag payong.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Papaya loves warm weather -- that's why it grows so easily here in the tropical Philippines!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe living things, such as animals and plants, as biotic factors and light, water, temperature, and soil type, as abiotic factors in an ecosystem
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a plant (papaya) and warm temperature, which are examples of a living thing and an abiotic factor, but it does not describe the concepts of biotic and abiotic factors or their roles in an ecosystem. It only states a simple fact about papaya's growth preference, providing no direct instructional support for the competency.

copy.en: Papaya loves warm weather -- that's why it grows so easily here in the tropical Philippines!
copy.tl: Mahilig sa init ang papaya -- kaya naman madali itong tumutubo dito sa tropikong Pilipinas!
copy.bis: Ganahan kaayo sa init ang kapayas -- mao nga sayon kini motubo dinhi sa tropikong Pilipinas!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Before paper, people wrote on leaves, tree bark, or stone! Then thin, light paper was invented, making writing and carrying so much easier!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from the home or the local community to identify a science invention and explain its impact on their everyday life
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a science invention (paper) and its impact, but it does not involve gathering information from the home or local community as required by the competency. It is general historical content, not a guided use of local sources.

copy.en: Before paper, people wrote on leaves, tree bark, or stone! Then thin, light paper was invented, making writing and carrying so much easier!
copy.tl: Bago ang papel, sumusulat ang mga tao sa dahon, balat ng kahoy, o bato! Nang naimbento ang manipis at magaang na papel, mas naging madali na ang pagsulat at pagdadala!
copy.bis: Sa wala pa'y papel, nagsulat ang mga tawo sa dahon, panit sa kahoy, o bato! Nang naimbento ang nipis ug gaan nga papel, mas dali na ang pagsulat ug pagdala!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Paper wasps chew wood mixed with saliva to make a paper-like nest
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes how paper wasps construct a nest, which is an example of shelter, but it does not teach the concept of basic needs (air, food, water, shelter) or ask students to identify them. It only incidentally mentions a nest, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en: Paper wasps chew wood mixed with saliva to make a paper-like nest — with hexagonal cells just like a bee's honeycomb!
copy.tl: Ginagawa ng paper wasp ang kanyang pugad mula sa kahoy na kinagat at laway, kaya parang papel ito—may hexagonal na selula tulad ng sa bubuyog!
copy.bis: Ang paper wasp maghimo sa iyang salag gikan sa gikuya nga kahoy ug laway, mao nga daw papel kini—naay hexagonal nga mga selula sama sa sa honeycomb sa bubuyog!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: choose a partner and stay together with them for a very long time.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes pair bonding and long-term association in parrots, which is a behavior of living things but does not directly teach the characteristics of growing, responding, or reproducing. It is only tangentially related to the competency.

copy.en: Many parrots, including the katala, choose a partner and stay together with them for a very long time.
copy.tl: Maraming loro, kasama ang katala, ay nagkakapares at nananatiling magkasama nang matagal na panahon.
copy.bis: Daghang loro, lakip ang katala, magtiayon ug magpabilin nga magkauban sa dugay nga panahon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: they use loud calls to talk with the rest of their flock
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to explore and describe some ways to use movement, sound, and light to send information between two people
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes animal communication using sound, but the competency specifically requires using movement, sound, or light to send information between two people. The card does not involve people or the guided activity of exploring ways to send information between people.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Parrots are noisy birds
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a living thing (parrot) and its behavior, but does not describe the characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce). It does not directly support the competency.

copy.en: Parrots are noisy birds — they use loud calls to talk with the rest of their flock.
copy.tl: Maingay ang mga loro — gumagamit sila ng malakas na huni para makipag-usap sa kanilang kawan.
copy.bis: Saba ang mga loro — mogamit sila og kusog nga tingog aron makig-istorya sa ilang panon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Density measures how tightly packed the particles of a substance are.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use diagrams and illustrations to describe the arrangement, spacing, and relative motion of the particles in each of the three states (phases) of matter
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions particles being packed, but does not use diagrams/illustrations and does not describe arrangement, spacing, relative motion, or the three states of matter as required by the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Iron is more densely packed than wood, so iron is heavier for the same size.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe matter as anything that has mass and takes up space
assignedReviews.reason: The card touches on mass and size but does not directly describe matter as anything that has mass and takes up space; it focuses on density, not the definition of matter.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Density measures how tightly packed the particles of a substance are.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe that particles are constantly in motion, have spaces between them, attract each other, and move faster as the temperature increases (or with the addition of heat)
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions particles being packed but does not describe constant motion, spaces between particles, attraction, or temperature effects as required by the competency.

copy.en: Density measures how tightly packed the particles of a substance are. Iron is more densely packed than wood, so iron is heavier for the same size.
copy.tl: Ang densidad ay sumusukat kung gaano kasiksik ang mga particle sa isang bagay. Ang bakal ay mas siksik kaysa kahoy kaya mas mabigat ito sa parehong sukat.
copy.bis: Ang densidad nagsukat kung unsa ka siksik ang mga particle sa usa ka substansya. Ang bakal mas siksik kaysa kahoy, busa ang bakal mas bug-at sa samang gidak-on.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It runs on a diesel engine that turns the wheels
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and demonstrate different ways to make objects move by natural causes, such as wind and water, or by people, such as pushing, pulling, rolling, and carrying
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a jeepney moving via a diesel engine, not the natural causes (wind, water) or human actions (pushing, pulling, rolling, carrying) that the competency asks students to explore and demonstrate. It shares the broad topic of movement but does not directly support the stated skill.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The jeepney is a Filipino passenger vehicle
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from the home or the local community to identify a science invention and explain its impact on their everyday life
assignedReviews.reason: The card identifies the jeepney as a Filipino vehicle but does not use information from home or the local community to identify it as a science invention or explain its impact on everyday life. It only names the vehicle and its basic operation, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en: The jeepney is a Filipino passenger vehicle! It runs on a diesel engine that turns the wheels to carry many people along a route.
copy.tl: Ang jeepney ay isang pampasaherong sasakyan sa Pilipinas! Umaandar ito gamit ang makinang diesel na nagpapaikot sa mga gulong para makapaghatid ng maraming tao.
copy.bis: Ang jeepney usa ka pampasaherong sakyanan sa Pilipinas! Modagan kini gamit ang makinang diesel nga magtuyok sa mga ligid aron makahatod ug daghang tawo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Pasteurization is gently heating milk to kill germs
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the factors affecting the rates of chemical reactions as applied in food preservation and materials production, control of fire, pollution, and corrosion
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions heating milk for food safety but does not explain any factor affecting the rate of a chemical reaction (e.g., temperature, concentration, surface area, catalyst). It only states that heating kills germs, which is not a chemical-reaction-rate concept.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Pasteurization is gently heating milk to kill germs
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe changes in properties of materials when exposed to certain changes in temperature, such as changes when wood or coal are burned
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a temperature-related change in milk (heating to kill germs), but it does not describe changes in the properties of materials when exposed to temperature changes, such as burning wood or coal. It is about microbial safety, not material property changes.

copy.en:
Why is milk heated before selling?

Pasteurization is gently heating milk to kill germs — that's what made milk so much safer to drink!
copy.tl:
Bakit iniinit ang gatas bago ibenta?

Ang pasteurisasyon ay bahagyang pag-init ng gatas para patayin ang mikrobyo — kaya naging mas ligtas na inumin ang gatas!
copy.bis:
Nganong gipainit ang gatas sa dili pa ibaligya?

Ang pasteurisasyon mao ang hinay nga pag-init sa gatas aron mapatay ang mikrobyo — mao nga nahimong mas luwas imnon ang gatas!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The patola (loofah) is a climbing vine vegetable that's cooked while young, and when left to ripen, its dried fibers become a natural scrubbing sponge.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify some useful things that people have made from non-living materials and describe what natural materials have been used to make the items
assignedReviews.reason: The competency concerns useful things made from non-living materials. The card describes a useful item (scrubbing sponge) made from dried plant fibers, which are living/natural materials, not non-living materials. No support for the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: when left to ripen, its dried fibers become a natural scrubbing sponge
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: compare the life cycles of mammals from birth to adulthood, birds from egg to a mature organism, and plants from seed to a young plant, and then to a mature plant
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a plant ripening from young to mature, but it does not compare life cycles of mammals, birds, or plants from seed to mature plant. It only touches on a single plant's maturation without the required comparison or stages.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: its dried fibers become a natural scrubbing sponge
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how changes in solid materials make them useful, such as when they are shaped, pressed, hammered, joined, or cut
assignedReviews.reason: The competency describes how changes in solid materials (shaped, pressed, hammered, joined, cut) make them useful. The card describes a natural drying process of plant fibers, not a change in solid materials through shaping or processing. It does not directly support the competency.

copy.en: The patola (loofah) is a climbing vine vegetable that's cooked while young, and when left to ripen, its dried fibers become a natural scrubbing sponge.
copy.tl: Ang patola ay gumagapang na halamang-gulay na niluluto kapag bata pa, at kapag pinatanda, ang tuyong hibla nito ay nagiging natural na panghilod.
copy.bis: Ang patola usa ka nagakatay nga utanon nga ginaluto samtang bata pa, ug kon tugotan nga mohinog, ang gahi nga himbis niini mahimong natural nga panghugas.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Sea turtles take so long to grow up
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use flow charts to compare the different stages in the life cycle of animals, such as a butterfly, frog, chicken, and human
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a life-cycle trait (slow growth) but does not use a flow chart or compare life-cycle stages as required by the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it takes many years for their numbers to recover
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: discuss as a class how threats to biodiversity can lead to species extinction
assignedReviews.reason: The card addresses population recovery after deaths, not a class discussion of threats to biodiversity leading to extinction. It does not directly support the competency's focus on threats and extinction.

copy.en: Sea turtles take so long to grow up that when some die, it takes many years for their numbers to recover.
copy.tl: Napakatagal bago tumanda ang pawikan, kaya kapag namatay ang ilan, matagal bago dumami muli ang kanilang bilang.
copy.bis: Dugay kaayo mahamtong ang pawikan, mao nga kon mamatay ang uban, dugay una modaghan pag-usab ang ilang gidaghanon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A pawikan is a big sea turtle that lives in the ocean!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a drawing or diagram to classify some Philippine animals and plants, based on their habitat: some live on land (terrestrial), live in water (aquatic) or fly in the air (aerial)
assignedReviews.reason: The card identifies a Philippine animal and its aquatic habitat, but the competency requires using a drawing or diagram to classify animals/plants by habitat. The card provides no drawing/diagram and does not perform classification, so it does not directly support the required activity.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A pawikan is a big sea turtle that lives in the ocean!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a sea turtle, which is a reptile, but the competency requires using a table to classify living things into named groups (e.g., reptiles). The card provides no table and does not classify the animal into any group, so it only shares vocabulary/subject matter.

copy.en:
What is a pawikan?

A pawikan is a big sea turtle that lives in the ocean!
copy.tl:
Ano ang pawikan?

Ang pawikan ay malaking pagong na nakatira sa dagat!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang pawikan?

Ang pawikan usa ka dako nga bao nga nagpuyo sa dagat!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The sea turtle's hard shell acts like a shield that protects its body.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the shell as an outer body part with a protective role, but the competency specifically requires identifying roles for movement and gathering food. Protection is not one of those roles, so the card does not directly support the competency.

copy.en: The sea turtle's hard shell acts like a shield that protects its body.
copy.tl: Ang matigas na kabibi ng pawikan ay parang kalasag na nagpoprotekta sa katawan nito.
copy.bis: Ang gahi nga kabhang sa pawikan nagasilbing taming nga nanalipod sa lawas niini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A pearl is made of calcium carbonate called nacre!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the properties of pure substances as: a. having fixed chemical composition, examples of which are elements and compounds, and b. that all the atoms of an element have a unique number of protons
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that a pearl is made of calcium carbonate (a compound), but it does not describe properties of pure substances such as fixed chemical composition, the distinction between elements and compounds, or the unique number of protons in atoms. It only mentions a material's composition without teaching the competency's concepts.

copy.en:
Ever wonder what pearls are made of?

A pearl is made of calcium carbonate called nacre! It’s the exact same material found inside a shell.
copy.tl:
Napag-isipan mo na ba kung ano ang gawa ng pearl?

Ang pearl ay gawa sa calcium carbonate na tinatawag na nacre! Ito ang mismong sangkap na makikita sa loob ng kabibe.
copy.bis:
Na-hanap ba nimo kung unsa ang hinimo sa pearl?

Ang pearl hinimo sa calcium carbonate nga gitawag og nacre! Kini ang samang sangkap nga makita sa sulod sa kabibe.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: wide, green leaves that we eat
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that pechay leaves are edible; it does not describe the role of leaves in getting water and nutrients from the soil, which is the focus of G3-L-5.

copy.en: Pechay (bok choy) is a vegetable with wide, green leaves that we eat.
copy.tl: Ang pechay ay isang gulay na may malapad at luntiang dahon na kinakain natin.
copy.bis: Ang pechay usa ka utanon nga adunay halapad ug lunhaw nga mga dahon nga atong gikaon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It's hard to stand, and heavy furniture might even move.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how the effects of earthquakes on communities depend on their magnitude
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes effects at a single intensity level (PEIS Intensity VI) but does not explain how effects depend on magnitude or compare different magnitudes. It provides an example of effects but not the dependency relationship required by the competency.

copy.en:
What happens during a PEIS Intensity VI (Very Strong) earthquake?

Many people get scared and run outside! It's hard to stand, and heavy furniture might even move.
copy.tl:
Ano ang nangyayari sa PEIS Intensity VI (Very Strong) na lindol?

Maraming natatakot at tumatakbo palabas! Nahihirapang tumayo nang tuwid, at maaaring gumalaw ang mabibigat na muwebles.
copy.bis:
Unsay mahitabo sa PEIS Intensity VI (Very Strong) nga linog?

Daghan ang nahadlok ug midagan pagawas! Naglisod sa pagtindog, ug ang bug-at nga muwebles mahimong molihok.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the pendulum clock was the most accurate timekeeper in the world
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: measure accurately the distance and time when things move using simple equipment
assignedReviews.reason: The card only mentions that a pendulum clock was an accurate timekeeper; it does not teach measuring distance and time when things move using simple equipment.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the pendulum clock was the most accurate timekeeper in the world
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from the home or the local community to identify a science invention and explain its impact on their everyday life
assignedReviews.reason: The card identifies a science invention (pendulum clock) and notes its historical accuracy, but it does not use information from the home or local community and does not explain the invention's impact on everyday life.

copy.en:
What was the world's most accurate timekeeper for hundreds of years?

From 1656 to the 1930s, the pendulum clock was the most accurate timekeeper in the world!
copy.tl:
Ano ang pinakatumpak na timekeeper sa mundo sa loob ng maraming taon?

Mula 1656 hanggang dekada 1930, ang relong may palawit (pendulum clock) ang pinakatumpak na timekeeper sa mundo!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang labing tukmang timekeeper sa kalibotan sa daghang tuig?

Gikan 1656 hangtod sa 1930s, ang relo nga adunay palawit (pendulum clock) mao ang labing tukmang timekeeper sa kalibotan!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: a pendulum rests at its lowest point, called the equilibrium or rest position
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe kinetic energy as the movement of objects or particles, and potential energy as energy stored due to the position of objects or particles
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the pendulum's rest/equilibrium position but does not mention kinetic energy, potential energy, or energy stored due to position. It shares the pendulum context but provides no direct instructional support for the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: a pendulum rests at its lowest point, called the equilibrium or rest position
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: measure and describe changes in the position of people or objects in relation to their original position, such as moving closer, farther, left, or right
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a single rest position, not changes in position relative to an original position, and does not involve measuring or describing movement closer, farther, left, or right. It only shares the general idea of position.

copy.en: When nothing pushes it, a pendulum rests at its lowest point, called the equilibrium or rest position.
copy.tl: Kapag walang humahatak, ang pendulum ay nakahinto sa pinakamababang punto, na tinatawag na equilibrium o rest position.
copy.bis: Kon walay nagduso niini, ang pendulum mopahulay sa pinakaubos nga punto, nga gitawag nga equilibrium o rest position.
